question: Should exec/process/node-host tool results redact secret-shaped output by default before the agent sees it, even though existing workflows may no longer receive byte-exact command output?
rationale: The patch closes a sensitive-output exposure, but choosing default redaction versus an explicit raw-output reveal path changes the agent-visible security boundary and compatibility contract.

options.title: Fix warning gap, then merge default redaction
options.body: Redact node-host warnings as part of this PR, accept redaction as the default agent-visible contract, and handle any raw-output reveal path separately with security review.

options.title: Require reveal control first
options.body: Keep the PR open until it adds a documented, tested, auditable way to request raw output when redaction is unacceptable.

options.title: Reject default redaction
options.body: Close or redirect the PR if maintainers decide byte-exact exec/process output must remain the default contract.

recommendation.title: Fix warning gap, then merge default redaction
recommendation.body: Redact node-host warnings as part of this PR, accept redaction as the default agent-visible contract, and handle any raw-output reveal path separately with security review.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current exec/process history signal and was already asked in the PR discussion for this security/product decision.
